svg.title: gov-tla B3 — Executive.tla: Article II and the administrative state, from the statutes Congress may pass to removal and acting officers, each rule a check TLC shows the model depends on and TLAPS proves
svg.desc: The Constitution creates no bureaus, so Init has none: Congress charters agencies from the constant Charters, and the model asks who appoints their officers, who may remove them, which branch they belong to, and how long an acting officer serves, beside the office of President under Amendment XXV and the pardon, treaty, war and convening powers. 208 TLC rows, every one as expected, and 814 proof obligations, every one proved, read from the two named results files when this diagram is built. The one liveness property, ActingEventuallyEnds, is checked, not proved; the witnesses and counterexamples are TLC's. This models the text's procedure: it is an exercise, not law.

svg.text: Checked means TLC explored every reachable state at the constants in the row list. Proved means TLAPS discharged every obligation for every value of the constants the module's named assumptions admit. Sampled means random simulation found no error, and is never cited as a check. "None of these is a claim about law or practice" (README § How the specs are written and checked). "This is an exercise, not law" (README, opening): the cases and statutes named below are the model's mutations and charters, not a statement of
what the law is.

text.tspan: The mechanism: three machines over one President, one Congress and the agencies it charters (

svg.text: Actions in code font as the module names them; violet names the mutation that removes a guard; a flag (congressAppointed, congressRemoved, warWithoutStatute, treatyShort) is raised by the one step that could violate its property. Solid arrows move authority or a seat; dashed arrows only remove one. At the rows' constants there is one agency, a1.
§3: "the President wrote to Congress" (
Inability).
"the President exercises the office".
Init starts here, and Elect,
PresidentVacates and Convict of
either officer return here.
§4: "VP and a majority of principal
officers".
"the President wrote that no inability
exists; four days to re-declare".
"they did; Congress decides, two-thirds
each".
①
②
③
④

⑧

① DeclareInability (§3): needs president # NoOne and VPToAct, a Vice President in office, which M_NOVP removes.
② DeclareAble from "SelfDeclared": under §3 the President's declaration ends the inability.
③ CabinetDeclares (§4): needs a President, a Vice President and Cabinet # {}, a head of a live Executive-branch agency.
④ DeclareAble from "CabinetDeclared": the President contests, and four days open.
⑤ DeclareAble from "Contested": the four days pass and the President resumes.
⑥ CabinetDeclares from "Contested": they re-declare, and the question goes to Congress.
⑦ CongressDecides(v) with TwoThirds(v): two-thirds of each House keeps the VP acting.
⑧ CongressDecides(v) with less: the President resumes. The four- and twenty-one-day windows are nondeterministic choice (README, Abstracted).

Art. I §8 cl. 18: ~Live(a) and Chartered(c); the charter's four fields are copied into Blank.
Bowsher: c.executesLaw => c.branch = "Executive", which M_GRH removes.
Slaughter: c.removal = "ForCause" => ~c.executesLaw, which M_HUMPHREY removes.
Buckley: c.vesting = "Congress" => ~c.executesLaw, which M_FECA removes.
AbolishAgency(a) returns the record to Blank.
From the statute: exists, branch, executesLaw, removal ("AtWill" or "ForCause"), vesting (President,
Head, Courts or Congress).
Seats, filled below: head, headNominee, acting, actingDays, inferior.
Decided at CreateAgency: ExecutionIsExecutive and UnitaryExecutive (module header).

text.tspan: Who may hold office, the trial, and the other powers (
The README's provisions table, every row, and what is abstracted (README §

svg.text: Art. II §1 — one President; the VP as Acting President has the full power
Elect, Executive, OneExecutive
Art. II §2 cl. 1 — pardons for offences against the United States, except in cases of impeachment
Pardon, PardonReaches, PardonScope
Art. II §2 cl. 2 — treaties need two-thirds of the Senate
Negotiate, RatifyTreaty, TreatyVote, TreatiesByTwoThirds
Art. II §2 cl. 2 — principal officers by advice and consent; inferior officers where Congress vests them (Buckley: never an executing officer in Congress)
NominateHead, ConfirmHead, AppointInferior, Appointer, Chartered, NoCongressionalAppointment
Art. II §3 — the President may convene Congress
Art. II §4, Art. I §§2–3 — impeachment, removal and disqualification
Impeach, Convict, Acquit, Disqualification
Art. I §6 cl. 2 — Incompatibility Clause
EligibleOfficer, Incompatibility
Art. I §8 — Congress creates agencies and declares war
CreateAgency, AbolishAgency, DeclareWar, WarIsCongressional
Amend. XXV §§3–4 — inability, voluntary and involuntary, and the contest before Congress
DeclareInability, CabinetDeclares, DeclareAble, CongressDecides
Bowsher v. Synar (1986) — an executing officer is in the Executive branch, and Congress removes, short of impeachment, only its own officers
Chartered, OwnOfficer, CongressRemovesHead, ExecutionIsExecutive, CongressDoesNotRemoveExecutors
Trump v. Slaughter (2026) — no for-cause protection for a body that executes the laws
Chartered, UnitaryExecutive
Federal Vacancies Reform Act — acting service only in a vacant office, and time-limited
ActAsHead, ActingTick, ActingExpires, ActingIsNotHead, ActingIsTemporary, ActingEventuallyEnds
The Constitution creates no bureaus. It refers to "executive Departments" and their "principal Officer[s]", but every department, agency and commission is a creature of
statute, so Init has none. Congress attempts statutes from the constant Charters. The rows use KnownCharters, six real statutes:
an executive department, CBO and the Sentencing Commission, which the checks in Chartered admit;
the FTC of Humphrey's Executor, the FEC of 1974 and the Comptroller General under Gramm–Rudman–Hollings, which they refuse.
vote counts (a vote is the strongest threshold it meets);
presentment, and who is pardoned;
the four- and twenty-one-day windows of Amendment XXV;
time, apart from an acting officer's day count.
Drawn as abstracted, never as modelled.

text.tspan: ABSTRACTED: the module header's paragraph, item by item (

svg.text: elections and the Electoral College (Elect picks a ticket)
presentment (a statute is the act of Congress passing it)
vote counts (a vote is the strongest threshold it meets, Votes; an action that needs a vote and has no Votes parameter is the vote that passes)
the XXV four- and twenty-one-day windows (nondeterministic choice)
who is pardoned (a pardon is recorded by the offence it reaches)
treaty negotiation detail
the Senate tries one impeachment at a time
courts and congressional appointers are always available
time, as an acting officer's day count that ActingTick may advance at any moment
The statutes Congress may attempt are the constant Charters; the rows use KnownCharters, six real ones, through CONSTANT Charters <- KnownCharters.
The Federal Reserve, which Slaughter left alone, and the Youngstown framework are not modelled.

text.tspan: The README's mutation table, every row, beside what each other record says the mutation breaks (the four right-hand columns are read at build time)

g.text: Chartered: for-cause protection only for a non-executing body
Chartered: no executing officer appointed by Congress
the FEC as first constituted (1974), struck in Buckley
Chartered: an executing body is in the Executive branch
the Comptroller General under Gramm–Rudman–Hollings (1985), struck in Bowsher
OwnOfficer: Congress removes only its own officers
the 1921 Act's removal by joint resolution
the pre-1998 reading that organic statutes displace the limit
Charles II's pardon of the Earl of Danby (1679)
WarAuthorised: only a statute changes the state of war

VPToAct: a §3 declaration needs a VP to act
OfficeVacant: acting service only in a vacant office

svg.text: No disagreement: for every mutation, the README's Breaks cell, the module header, the results file's Expected: line, the properties TLC found a counterexample to, and the theorems whose hypotheses exclude it name the same properties. The README's "Reverts to" column is drawn as it stands, "—" included: a mutation is earlier law, doctrine or practice, or no history at all.

text.tspan: Mutation × property: every INVARIANT and DEADLOCK row of

svg.text: 183 rows; each cell gives the verdict and its distinct states. An empty cell is a pair no row runs (Safety, TypeOK and the deadlock audit run under none only). The none row (blue) is the text. Treaty rows run at Treaties = {t1}, hence the larger counts; M_PREFVRA's run under DaysBound. Every COUNTEREXAMPLE is in a column the README's Breaks cell names, and every column it names has one: no cell is marked.
NoCongressionalAppointment is a flag rather than true by definition, since Congress may now be vested with appointment, as it is for CBO's director.
WarIsCongressional and CongressDoesNotRemoveExecutors are flags set at the violating step rather than action properties.
TreatiesByTwoThirds is new.
In Executive.tla, M_SAMEPERSON (one person as both President and Vice President) also breaks Disqualification. Convicting that person passes the presidency to
themself. The proof's inductive step for Convict needed President ≠ VP, and TLC confirms the counterexample.

text.tspan: What each mutation reverts to (module header, MUTATIONS)

svg.text: 9 are earlier law or practice: placemen in the Commons, the pre-1998 reading of the Vacancies Act, the FEC of 1974, Gramm–Rudman–Hollings, the 1921 Act's joint resolution,
Humphrey's Executor until Slaughter, Danby's pardon (1679), the Crown's prerogative, the draft of 6 August 1787.
5 say "No earlier text": M_ACTWHILEFILLED, M_DISQUAL, M_NOVP, M_SAMEPERSON, M_STATECRIME; the README's Reverts to cell for each is "—".
an agency created and one abolished;
a head confirmed and one removed by the President, and Congress removing its own officer;
an acting officer serving and one timing out;
Congress appointing a non-executing body's officer, a for-cause-protected head, and a disqualification;
a voluntary and an involuntary inability declaration, a contest before Congress sustained and one lost, and the VP succeeding;
war declared, a treaty ratified, a pardon, and the President convening Congress.

text.tspan: REACHABILITY WITNESSES: the module header's list (

svg.text: an agency created and one abolished, a head confirmed and one removed by the President, Congress removing its own officer, an
acting officer serving and timing out, Congress appointing (a non-executing body's officer), a for-cause-protected head, a
disqualification, a voluntary and an involuntary inability declaration, a contest before Congress sustained and one lost, the VP
succeeding, war declared, a treaty ratified, a pardon, the President convening Congress.
Each "must be VIOLATED under "none"" (its heading). The rows run state witnesses as INVARIANT rows and step witnesses as
PROPERTY rows (Expected: line).

A witness is checked, never proved: a run that reaches a state is evidence it is reachable at those constants (README § How …, What is not proved). TLC records no distinct-state count for a PROPERTY row's counterexample. "State predicates are INVARIANT rows; [][...]_vars ones, which name a step, are PROPERTY rows" (Executive.tla, before the witnesses).

text.tspan: , checked under the fair spec and shown to need both fairness conditions

g.text: Under ClockRuns and LimitBinds every acting officer's service ends.
Under ClockRuns and LimitBinds every acting officer's service ends.
Without ClockRuns the days need not pass: acting service can last for ever.
Without LimitBinds the limit can be reached and service not ended.
NoBehaviour == <>FALSE is violated, so the fair spec has a behaviour and the HOLDS is not vacuous.
NoBehaviour == <>FALSE is violated, so the fair spec has a behaviour and the HOLDS is not vacuous.

svg.text: ActingEventuallyEnds == \A a \in Agencies : (agency[a].acting # NoOne) ~> (agency[a].acting = NoOne): the Take Care Clause read with the FVRA.
SpecLive == Spec /\ ClockRuns /\ LimitBinds; SpecNoClock drops ClockRuns; SpecNoLimit drops LimitBinds. Each is weak fairness for every agency.
Spec has no fairness: the liveness claim is under SpecLive only (module header, LIVENESS).
Liveness. SpecLive adds ClockRuns (days pass) and LimitBinds (the Executive ends acting service at the limit). ActingEventuallyEnds holds under SpecLive, and fails
under SpecNoClock and under SpecNoLimit.
"a leads-to quantified over Agencies inside the temporal body, with fairness on ActingTick(a) and ActingExpires(a) for each a": the case the method's prover habits record as
having no sound route in this prover.
"checked by TLC at one agency and ActingLimit = 1 and 2, with each fairness condition shown necessary and the fair spec non-empty."
